workhorse-loop-runner run --dry-run
  Start the loop runner against the agent backend and the configuration the flags name.
  runs: workhorse-loop-runner run --dry-run --runs-dir {runs_dir} --params {params} --params-file {params_file} --cli {cli} --profile {profile} --config {config} --workspace {workspace} --context-file {context_file} --resume-run {resume_run}
  body: RunArgs
  0 → lines of text: the dry run walks the loop to its end, prints where its artifacts went, and finishes the run
  1 → Stderr: the flags name something the runner cannot find or read
  2 → Stderr: two flags that cannot be given together were given together
  carries: DryRun
    refuses 1 'error: --config {config}: no such file'
    refuses 2 'error: --cli and --profile are mutually exclusive — a profile carries its own `cli` field. Drop one of them.'
      why: A profile names its own backend, so a second one on the command line would have two answers.
    refuses 1 "error: resume run dir not found for '{resume_run}' (looked under <sandbox>/{where})"
    refuses 1 "error: unknown CLI backend '{cli}' (set AGENT_CLI, --cli or the config's default_cli to one of: claude, cline, codex, copilot, opencode)"
    refuses 1 "error: unknown profile '{profile}' in <sandbox>/config.toml (known: none defined)"
    refuses 1 'error: --params is not valid JSON: {json_problem}'
    refuses 1 'error: --params must be a JSON object (key→value map)'
    refuses 1 "error: cannot read --params-file {params_file}: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '{params_file}'"
    refuses 1 "error: --workspace {workspace}: unknown workspace '{workspace}'; known workspaces: (none)"
    refuses 1 'error: --context-file not found: {context_file}\nRun `make agent-install` to generate .agents/agents-context.json.'

workhorse-loop-runner control
  Steer one run of the loop runner: read its checkpoint, rewind it to an earlier state, or switch its backend.
  runs: workhorse-loop-runner control {verb} {name} --run {run} --to {to} --keep {keep} --param {param} --param-from-turn {param_from_turn} [--params] [--core] [--at-boundary] [--wait] --text {text}
  body: ControlArgs
  0 → lines of text (not compared: lines starting '  backup:'): the checkpoint is printed, or the rewind is applied and described
  1 → Stderr: the run, the verb or the arguments cannot be acted on, and the checkpoint is left as it was
  carries: SteerRun
    refuses 1 "error: no run dir for '{run}' (looked under <sandbox>/.agents/runs)\n  groom at http://127.0.0.1:9 not reachable"
      why: A name groom does not know either leaves the operator with the directory the lookup searched.
    refuses 1 'error: no unfinished run found under <sandbox>/.agents/runs — name one with --run'
    refuses 1 'error: {verb} takes no --to, --param, --param-from-turn or --keep'
      why: A flag typed after the wrong verb is an error, because silence would read as a request that worked.
    refuses 1 'error: {verb} takes no --params (it is `status --params`)'
    refuses 1 'error: {verb} takes no --core or --at-boundary'
    refuses 1 'error: {verb} takes no --wait (it is `stop --wait`)'
    refuses 1 'error: {verb} takes no --gate or --text'
    refuses 1 'error: rewind needs the state to move to: `control rewind --to STATE`'
    refuses 1 'error: rewind: <sandbox>/.agents/runs/loop-runner-{target} already finished (terminal)'
      why: A run that finished has no checkpoint left to move; only a stopped or failed run can be rewound.
    refuses 1 "error: --param wants NAME=VALUE, got '{param}'"
    refuses 1 "error: --param-from-turn: cannot read <sandbox>/.agents/runs/loop-runner-{target}/{turn_file}: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<sandbox>/.agents/runs/loop-runner-{target}/{turn_file}'"
    refuses 1 "error: rewind refused, checkpoint unchanged: LoopRunner has no state '{to}'. Known states: start. If it was renamed, declare @state(aliases=['{to}']) on the state that replaced it so runs checkpointed under the old name can resume."
      why: A checkpoint that names a state the flow no longer has could never be resumed, so the move is refused before it is written.
    refuses 1 "error: rewind refused, checkpoint unchanged: checkpoint gives state 'start' the parameter(s) {param_name}, which it does not have. Its parameters are: (none)."
    refuses 1 'error: rewind refused, checkpoint unchanged: --keep names {keep}, which the checkpoint does not hold. It holds: stale'
    refuses 1 'error: rewind refused, checkpoint unchanged: --keep names {keep}, which the checkpoint does not hold. It holds: (none)'
    refuses 1 'error: resume: <sandbox>/.agents/runs/loop-runner-{target} already finished (terminal)'
    refuses 1 "error: resume: no usable launch.json in <sandbox>/.agents/runs/loop-runner-{target} ([Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<sandbox>/.agents/runs/loop-runner-{target}/launch.json') — run `<workflow> run --resume-run <sandbox>/.agents/runs/loop-runner-{target}` by hand"
      why: Only a run that was started with a recorded launch can be relaunched from its directory.
    refuses 1 "error: {verb} takes no name (got '{name}')"
    refuses 1 'error: switch-cli needs the name to switch to, e.g. `control switch-cli claude`'
    refuses 1 'error: stop takes no --core or --at-boundary'

DryRunAndGraph
A person checks the install, rehearses the loop without an agent, and looks at the flow it walked. They read the
    version, run once into the default directory and once into another, print the flow as a graph, name it, and
    write both graphs to files.

AnswerTheInbox\nA run stopped at a gate and left two messages. The operator lists what is outstanding, lists everything, answers\n    the open one, and finds nothing outstanding any more. They then answer the message that already had an answer.

RewindAStoppedRun\nA run stopped at a gate with a stale parameter. The operator reads its checkpoint, moves it back to its start,\n    which drops the parameter and frees the gate, and reads the checkpoint again.

WrongTurns
An operator steers runs and gets it wrong. They look for a run when none exists, name a run that is not there,
    rewind one that ended, rewind to a state that is not there, hand rewind a bad parameter, type a flag after a verb
    that does not take it, resume a run that never launched, and answer a message that is not in the inbox. Each time
    the checkpoint stays as it was.

RunRefusals
A person starts a run with flags that cannot work. A backend the runner does not know, a backend together with a
    profile, a profile or config or workspace or context file that is not there, parameters that are not JSON or not an
    object, a parameters file that is missing, and a run to resume that is missing. The runner refuses each before it
    writes any run.
- **empty**: the working directory holds no run. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **parked**: a run stopped at a gate with two messages, one answered. Reached by: ParkARun ParkArgs().
- **replied**: the open message of the parked run was answered. Reached by: ParkARun ParkArgs(); workhorse-loop-runner inbox reply m1 'go ahead'.
- **rewound**: the parked run was moved back to its start. Reached by: ParkARun ParkArgs(); workhorse-loop-runner control rewind --to start.
- **finished**: the parked run is joined by a run that ended. Reached by: ParkARun ParkArgs(); FinishARun FinishArgs().
- **dry-run**: a dry run walked the loop to its end. Reached by: workhorse-loop-runner run --dry-run.
A run of the loop runner stops at a gate with two messages for its operator, one of them already answered.\ncarries: ParkByHand
A run of the loop runner ends, so its run record says it is terminal.\ncarries: FinishByHand
story: workhorse-book
elements: Run

The text of `--params` is judged as the runner judges it, by Python's JSON parser, so the refusal quotes the position of the first fault (`line 1 column 3 (char 2)`) and differs with leading spaces. `RunArgs.json_problem` carries the parser's own words. Text that parses to anything but an object is refused with the object message.
story: workhorse-book
elements: InboxReply, FileRecord

`inbox reply` stores the text as typed: no trimming, no case change (workhorse/workhorse/inbox.py::reply). The watch declares the strings `go ahead` for either message and `yes` for the second, so a reply of any other text leaves the message holding none of the declared strings. The model keeps exactly that, and does not guess a message's later `inbox read` after an undeclared text.
story: workhorse-book
elements: Replay

`replay` re-runs one recorded agent turn against a live backend. The sandbox has none, so the book plays only its refusals: a run that is not there, and a turn directory without a `turn.json`. `Service.unseen` says so for the inputs of `Replay`. Both `--run` and the turn are required by the command's parser, so the book declares both fields required and never sends the command without them.
story: workhorse-book
elements: Control

`control status` without `--params`, `stop`, `reload`, `questions`, `answer` and `switch-cli` with a backend name talk to the run's listener, and a run is live only while a backend drives it. The sandbox has none, so those verbs are reached only through their refusals: a verb that names no run, a switch with no backend, a stop with a scope it does not take. What the book plays in full is the offline half: `status --params` reads the checkpoint on disk, `rewind` rewrites it, and `resume` refuses a run that finished or never launched. The model therefore keeps a run's checkpoint and event log, and never a listener.
story: workhorse-book
elements: Run

The book plays `run` only with `--dry-run`, which is written into the argv as a word. A run without it drives a live agent backend (workhorse/workhorse/cli/run.py::run), which the sandbox does not provide and which would make the answer depend on the machine. The dry run walks the loop with a stand-in for every node, so the files it writes and the lines it prints are the same in every world. The refusals of `run` (an unknown backend, profile, workspace, config, params or context file) are played because the runner checks them before it starts anything.
story: workhorse-book
elements: Control, InboxRead, InboxReply, Replay, FileRecord

The seed holds no run, because a person gets one only by running the loop against a backend. A run stopped at a gate, with two messages in its inbox, one of them answered, is what a person finds after leaving a run overnight. `ParkARun` writes that run and `FinishARun` writes a finished one, so `control`, `inbox` and `replay` are played against runs the dry run cannot make. Both are listed in `Service.outside` and their actions accept a fixture that gives an example only while the run is missing, so the walk offers each event once.
story: workhorse-book
elements: Run

`workhorse-loop-runner ARGS` with no subcommand is `run ARGS` (workhorse/workhorse/cli/__init__.py, `_DEFAULT_COMMAND`). The book always spells `run` out, so the bare form is not a second command. An argparse usage error (exit 2) is reachable only through a flag combination the book does not build on purpose, and is not played.
story: workhorse-book
elements: Run

The runner asks the groom service about the story it works on. The sandbox sets GROOM_URL to http://127.0.0.1:9, a port nothing listens on, so the lookup fails the same way in every world and the machine's own groom does not answer. HOME and STABLEMATE_CONFIG point inside the sandbox for the same reason: the home config is a file the seed writes (`config_version = 2`), so no profile, workspace or backend list comes from the person running the book.
story: workhorse-book
elements: Control, InboxRead

A rewind prints `  backup:  <path>` and the path carries a time stamp, so the line is opaque and the model does not say it. Every `inbox read` header (`[m1] <time> (outstanding)`) is opaque for the same reason: a reply stamps its message with the time of the reply, and the header shows it. The body lines and the `  -> reply` lines are compared. The `replied` marker of a header is therefore not judged; whether a message is answered is judged by the reply line and by the inbox file the watch reads.
story: none
elements: Run, Dot, Control, Replay

The sandbox plays `run` with `--dry-run` only, which walks the flow with a stand-in for every node. The command still reaches the whole loop runtime when a live backend drives it: the agent runner and its backends, the worktree cuts, the gate parking, the worklist and the telemetry. The `source` of `Run` names every module of the package except the ones below, so a change to the runtime is a reason to replay the command, even where the dry run only imports the module.

`Dot` also names the graph reader it draws from, `Control` names the listener side that a live run serves (workhorse/workhorse/control.py, workhorse/workhorse/reload.py) next to the offline rewind, and `Replay` names the turn record it re-reads.

Four things are left out of every element. The package `__init__` files that only re-export, the READMEs and the vendored copy of the shared core hold no behaviour a command reaches. `workhorse/workhorse/testing.py` is a set of helpers for the tests of a workflow author, and no command calls it.
story: workhorse-book
elements: Run

The runner prints the paths of the run directory it works in, and the surface writes the sandbox path back as `<sandbox>` in everything the program printed. The seed names the directory `acme` so the working directory the runner resolves, its basename, is the same in every world. Paths a message prints are written `<sandbox>/.agents/runs/loop-runner-<name>`.
story: workhorse-book
elements: Version

`version` prints the number of the installed package, which changes at every release. Every digit is declared opaque, so the answer is judged as one line of text that the model does not predict. The number itself is not a claim of the book.
story: none
elements: Look, FileRecord

After every step the book reads the files a command may write: the checkpoint, run record, event log and inbox of each run under `.agents/runs` or beside it, and any `.dot` file `dot -o` leaves. A row holds only which of the declared strings a file contains, never its whole text, because the files carry time stamps and run digests that differ in every world. `Look` names the two writers whose effect the strings judge, the rewind that rewrites a checkpoint and logs its backup (workhorse/workhorse/rewind.py) and the reply that stamps an inbox message (workhorse/workhorse/inbox.py).
